why: A = case1Map_zero ∧ case1Map_one ∧ theoremA_case1 (universes 0), all with every X_n CLOSED; B (blind) uses the CORRECTED last piece h^{n+1}_{(4t−3)u} (so the misprint (4−3t)u is not copied; no not_B) and has NO closedness: (a) f_Σ is a homotopy equivalence, (b) Milnor's formula h_u is a continuous homotopy K: k₀ ≃ k₁, (c) k₀ ≃ f_Σ, (d) k₁ has the VA.9 properties. B ⇒ A: theoremA_case1 is B(a) on closed sets (glue tel ≃ₜ telescope; resC and restrictTo are defeq); case1Map_zero (the EQUALITY h₀ = f_Σ ∘ R₂) and case1Map_one concern the project's own map case1Map and are re-proved outright. A ⇒ B: B is TRUE without closedness. (a) uses A: theoremA_case1 applied to the space X_Σ and its (always closed) truncations, f_Σ|X^m_Σ ≃ id via (T2), then Lemma 2.2 + of_telescopeMap. (b)–(d) are proved directly, not from A (A's case1Map needs closed sets for (T3) pasting): h_u is continuous for ANY increasing S because near an integer level m every point lies over X_m and h_u only involves h^m there (last piece of strip m−1 and first piece of strip m paste along τ = m), while inside a strip the project's continuous_case1Fun applies. So B is strictly more general than A (Case 1 and Milnor's homotopy h_u without closedness, contrary to the project's remark that Case 1 'as he states it' needs closed X_i — only the inverse g of VA.9 does); A's extra content is the exact identity h₀ = f_Σ ∘ R₂.
